title: EvoLM: In Search of Lost Language Model Training Dynamics

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Abstract states: 'we release selected pre-trained and post-trained models along with portions of the training datasets and partial evaluation scripts. However, due to proprietary portions of the dataset... full training pipelines and all data cannot be fully released publicly at this time.' Introduction contribution bullet claims: 'Open-sourcing 100+ LMs trained from scratch with 1B and 4B parameters and their training data for all stages'. The claim that training data for all stages is openly released contradicts the partial disclosure described in the abstract.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1, paragraph: 'Table 1 presents a filtered comparison favoring smaller models...'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paragraph states: Table 1 presents a filtered comparison favoring smaller models... ignoring the inherently higher FLOPs and parameter updates... resulting in incomplete and cherry-picked evidence that exaggerates smaller models’ competitive edge while underreporting larger models’ potential. This reads as an external critique or an unreviewed internal note. Later the paper relies on Table 1 as valid evidence ('As Table 1 illustrates...') and draws conclusions from it, creating a direct internal inconsistency and undermining the credibility of the presented findings.

In the main text, continued pretraining uses FineMath and cites reference [2] (Allal et al., SmolLM2). Reference [38] is Penedo et al. (FineWeb) and does not describe FineMath. The dataset description wrongly attributes FineMath to the wrong publication.

The text states that a modest replay budget 'around 5%' optimally balances retention. However, Table 2 shows the best-performing configuration uses 8B replay out of a total 50B CPT tokens, i.e., 16% replay, not 5%. Takeaway 3 similarly says 'e.g., 5%'. The reported optimal percentage is factually inconsistent with the experimental data.
